action: No action needed yet; watch for a Visa or supplier notice naming the provider, and treat the gang's JPMorgan claim as unconfirmed.
date_note: The article's publication date was not visible; it refers to the JPMorgan outage of November 16, so November 17 is the best supported day.
exec: Supplier incident touching Visa; attacker claims about Visa and JPMorgan data remain unverified.
plain: A hacking gang says it has data from Visa and JPMorgan. Visa says the problem was at an outside supplier in Asia Pacific and its own systems and card numbers were not affected.
summary: The n0n extortion gang listed Visa and JPMorgan Chase as victims with a 48-hour leak countdown, giving few details. Visa told Cybernews the incident was at an unnamed third-party provider in Asia Pacific, that its own systems were not involved and that there is no indication card numbers were affected. The claim against JPMorgan is unconfirmed; the bank says there is no evidence linking its outage, attributed to a software bug, to a cyberattack.
title: Visa says incident was at an Asia Pacific third-party provider after n0n gang lists it and JPMorgan

validation.note: Only Cybernews reports Visa's statement; the attacker's claims about Visa and JPMorgan data are unverified.
